source_locator.quote:
Self-attention scales quadratically with the number of tokens,
making high-resolution images and multi-frame videos particularly expensive and often impractical on compute- and memory-constrained mobile platforms.

claims.text: DiT self-attention scales quadratically with token count, making high-resolution images and multi-frame videos costly and often impractical on compute- and memory-constrained mobile platforms.

source_locator.quote: CoReDiT uses a linear-time spatial coherence score to estimate local redundancy in the latent token lattice and skips high-coherence (redundant) tokens in self-attention.

claims.text: CoReDiT uses a linear-time spatial-coherence score to identify locally redundant latent tokens and skips high-coherence tokens in self-attention.

source_locator.quote: To maintain a dense representation and avoid visual discontinuities, we reconstruct skipped attention outputs via coherence-guided aggregation of spatially neighboring retained tokens.

claims.text: The method reconstructs skipped attention outputs with coherence-guided aggregation of spatially neighboring retained tokens to keep a dense representation and avoid discontinuities.

source_locator.quote: We further introduce a progressive, block-adaptive pruning schedule that increases pruning gradually and allocates larger budgets to blocks and denoising steps with higher redundancy.

claims.text: A progressive block-adaptive schedule gradually increases pruning and assigns larger pruning budgets to blocks and denoising steps with higher redundancy.

source_locator.quote: At r = 40 % r=40\% average pruning, CoReDiT reduces self-attention FLOPs by 48% (24% total FLOPs) while maintaining quality close to the baseline (FID 28.7 vs. 27.3).

claims.text: For PixArt-alpha-1024 at 40% average pruning, CoReDiT reports 48% lower self-attention FLOPs and 24% lower total FLOPs, with FID 28.7 versus 27.3 for the baseline.

source_locator.quote:
Tab.   2 reports both self-attention and end-to-end latency on Nvidia H100 GPUs under two attention backends: (i) highly-optimized kernels xformers.memory_efficient_attention (Efficient Attn) and (ii) PyTorch native attention implementations (Native Attn).
With 45% pruning, CoReDiT reduces self-attention latency by 26% under the efficient attention backend, but end-to-end latency improves by 11% because non-attention components (e.g., FFN/MLP, I/O, and kernel launch overheads) remain unchanged.

claims.text: On Nvidia H100 GPUs with memory-efficient attention, 45% pruning reduces self-attention latency by 26% but end-to-end latency by 11%, with unchanged non-attention work limiting the total gain.

source_locator.quote:
Beyond GPU inference, Fig.   8 shows per-block latency on Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite NPUs.
At 50% pruning, CoReDiT achieves up to 1.72 × 1.72\times per-block speedup at 1600 resolution.

claims.text: On Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite NPUs, CoReDiT reports up to 1.72x per-block speedup at 1600 resolution with 50% pruning.

source_locator.quote: Notably, the baseline PixArt- α \alpha encounters out-of-memory (OOM) error at resolutions above 1600, whereas CoReDiT runs up to 1920 resolution and matches the baseline latency at 1600.

claims.text: The baseline PixArt-alpha runs out of memory above 1600 resolution, while CoReDiT runs at up to 1920 and matches baseline latency at 1600.

source_locator.quote: As shown in Tab.   3 , at an average pruning level of 23%, CoReDiT reduces self-attention FLOPs by 32% (25% total FLOPs), translating into a 22% reduction in self-attention latency and a 15% end-to-end latency reduction (batch size 32, memory-efficient attention).

claims.text: For PixArt-Sigma-2048 at 23% average pruning, CoReDiT reports 32% lower self-attention FLOPs, 25% lower total FLOPs, 22% lower self-attention latency, and 15% lower end-to-end latency at batch size 32 with memory-efficient attention.

source_locator.quote: We attribute part of this gap to a resolution-domain mismatch: our fine-tuning dataset is at 1K (upscaled to 2K) while evaluation uses native 2K images.

claims.text: The PixArt-Sigma-2048 fine-tuning data are 1K images upscaled to 2K, whereas evaluation uses native 2K images, creating a resolution-domain mismatch that the authors say contributes to the remaining quality gap.

source_locator.quote: We prune only spatial transformer blocks and achieve a 39% self-attention FLOPs reduction (8% total FLOPs at the full-model level) as shown in  Tab.   4 .

claims.text: For MagicDrive-V2, pruning only spatial transformer blocks yields a reported 39% self-attention FLOPs reduction and 8% full-model FLOPs reduction.

source_locator.quote: Currently, CoReDiT is applied only to spatial transformer blocks in which each frame is processed independently. Consequently, we observed a drop in FVD, which reflects temporal consistency in the generated video.

claims.text: The MagicDrive-V2 application prunes only independently processed spatial blocks, and the authors report a drop in FVD reflecting reduced temporal consistency.

method: CoReDiT prunes locally redundant tokens before self-attention using a linear-time spatial-coherence score, reconstructs skipped outputs from retained neighbors, and learns a progressive block- and timestep-adaptive pruning schedule during lightweight fine-tuning.
problem: Diffusion Transformers incur high self-attention compute and memory costs for high-resolution image and multi-frame video generation, limiting deployment on constrained mobile systems.
warnings: The frozen paper does not name an EDGE CFP topic, so no workshop-topic mapping is asserted.
The Snapdragon result is reported as a per-block latency speedup and should not be treated as an end-to-end mobile speedup.
